elementTypes.label: Joint
elementTypes.description: A kinematic pair joining two bodies; its kind sets its freedom (revolute and prismatic one, pin in slot and cam contact two).

elementTypes.label: Fixed Frame
elementTypes.description: The fixed frame (link 1), drawn hatched at each fixed pivot; every frame symbol is the same body.

elementTypes.label: Ternary Link
elementTypes.description: A rigid body joining three or more joints, drawn as a plate.

elementTypes.label: Cam
elementTypes.description: A cam body.

elementTypes.label: Follower
elementTypes.description: A cam follower body.

elementTypes.label: Kinematic Spring
elementTypes.description: A spring between two bodies; it adds no body and no joint to the count.

elementTypes.label: Drive Motor
elementTypes.description: The prime mover driving the transmission.

elementTypes.label: Driven Load
elementTypes.description: The driven machine at the end of the transmission.

elementTypes.label: Gear
elementTypes.description: A gear seen from the side, its pitch line through it; external meshes turn the other way, internal ones the same way.

elementTypes.label: Pulley
elementTypes.description: A belt pulley.

elementTypes.label: Sprocket
elementTypes.description: A chain sprocket.

elementTypes.label: Friction Wheel
elementTypes.description: A friction wheel driving another by contact.

elementTypes.label: Shaft Coupling
elementTypes.description: A coupling joining two shafts.

elementTypes.label: Clutch
elementTypes.description: A clutch; disengaged, it passes no motion on.

properties.label: Actuation
properties.description: How it is worked: mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic or electric.

elementTypes.label: Brake
elementTypes.description: A brake on a shaft.

elementTypes.label: Bearing
elementTypes.description: A bearing supporting a shaft.

elementTypes.label: Effort Source (Se)
elementTypes.description: A source of effort (force, voltage, pressure).

properties.label: Parameter
properties.description: The element's parameter (m, k, b, the source value).

elementTypes.label: Flow Source (Sf)
elementTypes.description: A source of flow (velocity, current, volume flow).

properties.label: Parameter
properties.description: The element's parameter (m, k, b, the source value).

elementTypes.label: Modulated Effort Source (MSe)
elementTypes.description: An effort source set by a signal.

properties.label: Parameter

elementTypes.label: Modulated Flow Source (MSf)
elementTypes.description: A flow source set by a signal.

properties.label: Parameter
properties.description: The element's parameter (m, k, b, the source value).

elementTypes.label: Bond Resistance (R)
elementTypes.description: A resistive element (damper, resistor).

properties.label: Parameter
properties.description: The element's parameter (m, k, b, the source value).

elementTypes.label: Bond Capacitance (C)
elementTypes.description: A storage element of effort (spring, capacitor).

properties.label: Parameter

elementTypes.label: Bond Inertia (I)

properties.description: The element's parameter (m, k, b, the source value).

elementTypes.label: Bond Transformer (TF)
elementTypes.description: A transformer between two bonds (lever, gear pair).

properties.label: Parameter
properties.description: The element's parameter (m, k, b, the source value).

elementTypes.label: Gyrator (GY)
elementTypes.description: A gyrator between two bonds (motor constant).

properties.label: Parameter
properties.description: The element's parameter (m, k, b, the source value).

elementTypes.label: 0-Junction
elementTypes.description: A common-effort junction.

elementTypes.label: 1-Junction
elementTypes.description: A common-flow junction.

elementTypes.label: Transfer Function Block
elementTypes.description: A block with a transfer function; mark it dynamic when it holds state.

properties.label: Transfer function
properties.description: The block's transfer function (G, Kp + Ki/s, 1/(s + 1)); empty uses its name.

properties.label: Dynamic
properties.description: The block holds state (it has poles), so a loop through it is not algebraic.

elementTypes.label: Gain Block
elementTypes.description: A constant gain.

properties.label: Gain
properties.description: The gain; empty uses its name.

elementTypes.label: Integrator
elementTypes.description: An integrator (1/s).

elementTypes.label: Time Delay
elementTypes.description: A time delay.

properties.label: Gain
properties.description: Its transfer function; empty is e^-sT.

elementTypes.label: Saturation
elementTypes.description: A limiter; the loop treats it as a gain of one.

elementTypes.label: Summing Junction
elementTypes.description: Adds its signed inputs; each signal in carries + or -.

elementTypes.label: Signal Branch Point
elementTypes.description: Where one signal is taken to several places.

elementTypes.label: Loop Input
elementTypes.description: The input of the block diagram (the reference).

elementTypes.label: Loop Output
elementTypes.description: The output of the block diagram.

relationshipTypes.label: Kinematic Link
relationshipTypes.description: A binary link between two joints; a link touching the frame or a plate is part of that body.

relationshipTypes.label: Shaft
relationshipTypes.description: Components joined by shaft segments turn together.

relationshipTypes.label: Gear Mesh
relationshipTypes.description: Two gears (or friction wheels) in contact.

relationshipTypes.label: Belt
relationshipTypes.description: A belt between two pulleys; a crossed belt turns the other way.

relationshipTypes.label: Bond
relationshipTypes.description: A power bond; the half arrow points the way positive power flows, the stroke marks causality.

properties.label: Causal stroke
properties.description: The end the causal stroke is at: start or end (Assign Causality sets it).

relationshipTypes.label: Signal Line
relationshipTypes.description: A signal; into a summing junction it carries a sign.

rules.description: A mechanism can move (mobility above zero).
A planar mechanism uses planar pairs.
The transmission is one connected drive.
Every shaft runs in a bearing.
Gears and sprockets give their tooth count.
Every way round a loop gives the same ratio.
Every bond has a causal stroke.
A 0-junction has one effort setter; a transformer passes causality through.
A 1-junction has one flow setter; a gyrator turns causality round.
A block input takes one signal.
Signals into a summing junction are signed.

rulesets.label: Kinematic diagram
rulesets.description: Joints, frame, mobility and planar pairs of a mechanism skeleton (ISO 3952-1).

rulesets.label: Power transmission
rulesets.description: One connected drive, shafts in bearings, tooth counts and consistent ratios (ISO 3952-2 and -3).

rulesets.label: Bond graph
rulesets.description: Causal strokes and the junction, source and storage causality rules (textbook convention).

rulesets.label: Control block diagram
rulesets.description: Block inputs, signed summing junctions, no dangling signals and no algebraic loops (textbook convention).

variants.label: ISO 3952
variants.description: The ISO 3952 kinematic symbols (no ANSI or IEEE kinematic symbol set exists, so this is the only one).

templates.label: Kinematic Diagram
templates.description: A mechanism skeleton to the ISO 3952 symbols: joints, links and the frame, with its mobility checked as you draw.

templates.label: Power Transmission
templates.description: Motors, shafts, gears, belts and chains to the load, with ratios traced along the drive.

templates.label: Bond Graph
templates.description: Sources, storage, resistance and junctions joined by power bonds, with causality assigned and checked.

templates.label: Control Block Diagram
templates.description: Blocks, summing junctions and signals of a control loop, with its transfer function by Mason's formula.

examples.label: Four-Bar Linkage
examples.description: A crank, coupler and rocker on two fixed pivots: four bodies, four revolute pairs, mobility 1.

examples.label: Slider-Crank
examples.description: A crank driving a slider through a connecting rod: three revolute pairs and one prismatic pair.

examples.label: Gearbox
examples.description: A motor through a coupling into two gear pairs on bearings (20 to 40, then 15 to 45) and a belt to a conveyor: 1 to 6 overall.

examples.label: Mass-Spring-Damper
examples.description: A force on a mass held by a spring and a damper, as a bond graph on one 1-junction with causality assigned.

examples.label: PI Control Loop
examples.description: A unity feedback loop: a PI controller ahead of the plant, the output fed back to the summing junction.
